issues.legal_issue: A municipal charge imposed under a licensing provision cannot be treated as a property tax merely because the licensed business is conducted on land or in a building.
material_facts: The municipality increased charges imposed on hotel operators under a provision authorising licence fees.
The licensing provision was in a part of the statute separate from the taxation provisions, and the statute distinguished licence fees from property taxes.
The municipality defended the increased charge as a tax on land and buildings rather than relying on its original claim that the charge was a fee for services.
The licensing schedule covered a range of occupations, including activities with only an incidental connection to land or buildings.
issues.conclusion: The charge under the licensing provision was not a tax on land or buildings and could not be upheld as one.
issues.legal_principle: The nature of a levy is determined from the provision’s terms and the statute read as a whole; its label and location are relevant but not conclusive. The Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920 separately addressed property taxation in section 78 and licensing in section 321(2). Liberty Cinema cautions that statutory location alone does not determine whether a levy is a tax or fee, while Ajoy Kumar supports taxing land by reference to its use only where the tax is in substance imposed on the land. The broad range of activities in Schedule V made it untenable to treat every licensing charge as a land tax based on its connection to premises.

predicates.municipal_licence_charge_challenged: A person challenged a charge imposed by a municipality in connection with a licence to carry on an activity.
predicates.charge_imposed_under_business_licensing_: The municipality imposed the charge under a power to regulate or license a business rather than under a power expressly directed to taxing property.
predicates.licensing_and_taxation_provisions_are_di: The statute treated licensing charges and property taxes in separate provisions or parts of its scheme.
predicates.charge_attaches_to_business_licence: The charge was imposed for the business licence rather than directly as a tax on the land or building.
predicates.scheduled_activities_have_only_incidenta: The licensed activities included occupations whose connection to land or buildings could be merely incidental.

issues.definition: When a challenged municipal charge is imposed through a distinct business-licensing power and attaches to the licence or to activities only incidentally connected with land, the charge is not a property tax.

issues.legal_issue: A municipality may impose a property tax on land or buildings by taking account of their use for hotel or restaurant business.
material_facts: The municipality argued that the charge on hotel operators could be sustained as a tax on land and buildings.
The Court distinguished the validity of a genuine property tax based on hotel use from the charge at issue, which was imposed on a business licence.
issues.conclusion: A municipality may tax property at a chosen rate, and use of land or buildings for a hotel or restaurant can provide a sufficient connection for such a tax, subject to other legal impediments.
issues.legal_principle: Entry 49 of List II of the Seventh Schedule permits taxation of land and buildings, and the legislative entries are interpreted broadly. A property tax may take account of the use to which the property is put. The Court relied on Ajoy Kumar v. Local Board, which held that land use could supply a sufficient nexus for a tax on land.

predicates.municipal_property_tax_case: The dispute concerns a municipality’s imposition of a tax on property.
predicates.tax_imposed_on_land_or_building: The charge is imposed in substance on the land or building, rather than merely on a licence to conduct a business.
predicates.property_used_for_hotel_or_restaurant_bu: The land or building is used to operate a hotel or restaurant.

issues.definition: A municipal tax imposed on land or a building may take account of the property’s use for hotel or restaurant business.

issues.legal_issue: A municipality cannot avoid mandatory procedures for imposing or enhancing taxes by imposing a charge under a licensing provision and then characterising it as a tax.
material_facts: The municipality had not followed the statutory procedure for imposing taxes, including inviting and considering objections to an enhancement.
The municipality sought to defend the increased licensing charge as a tax on land and buildings.
The statutory tax procedure was mandatory, while the increased charge had been imposed under the separate licensing provision.
issues.conclusion: The increased charge could not be sustained as a tax because the mandatory tax-imposition procedure had not been followed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 78(3) of the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920 prescribed mandatory procedures for imposing taxes, including prior invitation and consideration of objections to an enhancement. The municipality could not use section 321(2) to impose a charge as a disguised tax and thereby frustrate those protections. The Court relied on Atlas Cycle Industries v. Haryana concerning mandatory compliance with tax-imposition procedure.

predicates.municipal_tax_imposition_challenged: A challenge concerns a municipality’s charge that the municipality seeks to sustain as a tax.
predicates.tax_procedure_requires_notice_and_consid: The governing law requires prior notice and consideration of objections before a tax is imposed or enhanced.
predicates.municipality_did_not_follow_required_tax: The municipality failed to carry out the required notice and objection procedure.
predicates.municipality_seeks_to_treat_licensing_ch: The municipality seeks to characterise a charge imposed under its licensing power as a tax.

issues.definition: When a municipality seeks to sustain a licensing charge as a tax but has not followed mandatory procedures for imposing taxes, the charge cannot be upheld as a tax.
